prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Production animation underpainting, not concept art.
The supplied cropped image is the exact edit target. Keep the ENTIRE image framing, camera, all stone surfaces, golden front curved wheel rim, bronze axle cap, water curtain on the right and foreground stone ledge EXACTLY as the supplied image. No zoom, no repositioning, no change of perspective or lighting.
Remove ONLY the four large golden-brown horizontal paddle boards projecting rightwards behind the front curved rim. Paint their newly exposed hidden surfaces so the wheel can be animated with separate replacement paddle attachments.
Behind these removed paddles there must be the solid dark warm-brown WOODEN CYLINDRICAL CORE of the wheel, with restrained darker wood grain and soft occlusion shadows under the front curved gold rim. It is the shaded curved cylindrical shell connecting the front wheel side to the back side, NOT a turquoise archway, empty hole or separate visible second wheel. Maintain the wheel's original compact volume, original dark brown gaps, original shadows and original radius. The wooden cylindrical shell is smoothly rotationally symmetric, without conspicuous permanent slats or protruding boards.
Keep the thick golden near-side curved rim and bronze axle untouched. Keep the narrow wooden shaft and dark spokes near the axle behind this rim. Do not introduce an extra circular wheel, new spokes, gear teeth, visible paddles, new plumbing or extra objects. Paint complete formerly hidden brown wood wherever a board was removed. The right thin cascade remains beautiful painterly luminous aqua as in the input.
Same hand-painted game sprite style, same dark teal/brown outlines and rounded edges. Preserve background transparency where already transparent. No text, diagram or sheet. This image is a registration-preserving local edit used as the underlayer of the original sprite.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Production texture attachments for the exact wooden waterwheel in the supplied close-up. Match THIS painted wood, its muted honey-brown color, creamy golden bevel, soft low-frequency brush shading, rounded corners, and dark brown outline. Not generic glossy icon art.
Create one transparent square source atlas with exactly THREE horizontally elongated isolated wood surfaces, stacked in THREE equally spaced rows. Each complete attachment is centered in its row, takes about 75% of canvas width, has transparent margins, no shadows outside the attachment, no text, no frames or diagrams. All surfaces belong to the same compact thick wooden paddle plank in the original waterwheel.
TOP ROW: complete front broad face of one paddle plank, directly face-on for rig texturing, width:height 3.2:1. Gently rounded chunky ends, lightly curved/beveled upper golden edge, honey/caramel wood front face shaded darker toward the bottom, restrained horizontal grain. Paint the complete left end that the original wheel rim hides. Do not bake an oblique camera view into the texture. No axle, wheel ring, stones, water or mounting hardware.
MIDDLE ROW: matching complete back broad face of that same plank, identical proportions, matte medium warm brown, subtly darker than the front, full hidden face and clean rounded contour. No decorative bands or symbols.
BOTTOM ROW: matching narrow top/edge face of the same plank, directly face-on as an elongated rounded rectangle, width:height 7:1, soft pale golden brown upper-left highlight and restrained depth shading. Same length as the other planks.
Retain the original softly painted fantasy game aesthetic and thick, functional, hand-crafted wooden paddles. Avoid plastic shine, huge white specular bands, orange neon color, metallic reflections, black drop shadows, outlines thicker than the reference, perspective skew, and detached extra parts. True transparent RGBA background.
